question: In Italy, 4.9 million people – approximately 10 % of the electorate – are at risk of being unable to exercise their rights in the June 2024 European elections. This mainly affects students and workers aged between 18 to 35 who reside abroad or in a different part of Italy than their municipality of origin.

Travelling back to their municipality in order to vote, as required by Italian law, entails buying expensive tickets. Current Italian legislation provides for partial reimbursement. However, some of the conditions attached to these reimbursements, such as opting for long-distance trains or flights operated by the national airline, severely reduce their effectiveness, given the high base prices.

Given that Articles 10 and 14 of the Treaty on European Union, Article 20(2)(b) of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and Article 39 of the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the EU clearly enshrine the right of EU citizens to participate in the democratic life of the Union, and that Article 1(4) of Council Decision (EU, Euratom) 2018/994 gives Member States the option to set up advance voting, postal voting and electronic and internet voting for the European elections: 1.
Does the lack of valid solutions to overcome these obstacles constitute an infringement of EU law?
What urgent measures does the Commission intend to take to put an end to this violation?
answer: Subject to certain basic principles, such as those laid down in Articles 2 and 10 of the Treaty on European Union, Member States are competent and responsible for laying down the specific procedures under which their nationals residing abroad or outside their municipality of origin can participate in elections.

As regards elections to the European Parliament, national electoral procedures must also comply with the principles set out in the Act concerning the election of the members of the European Parliament by direct universal suffrage (the 1976 Electoral Act) (1).

Article 8 of the 1976 Electoral Act provides that, subject to the provisions of that act, the electoral procedure is to be governed in each Member State by its national provisions. The 1976 Electoral Act does not contain any specific provision on advance voting, postal voting or online voting. Such possibilities are therefore subject to national rules.

Council Decision 2018/994 (2) would amend the 1976 Electoral Act to include some relevant provisions, but it has not been brought into force. In December 2023, the Commission adopted a recommendation on inclusive and resilient elections (3), as part of the ‘Defence of Democracy’ package (4), the aims of which include to promote high voter turnout, and easy and equal exercise of electoral rights.
In its European Cooperation Network on Elections, the Commission also supports exchanges among Member States on the use of various complementary voting methods.
